capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia Model S: the 40 kWh car was delivered as a 60 kWh pack software-limited to 40 kWh (2013). VIN reference lists the 51-60 kWh tier for 2012-2013.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: Software limit of 40 kWh on the 60 kWh pack (Wikipedia Model S). The 2013 "40" label is the 60 kWh hardware with a 40 kWh software cap.

chemistry.notes: EVSpecifications 2017-2018 Model S/X: NCA (Panasonic NCR18650A, LiNiCoAlO2); Wikipedia Model S: NCA cathode.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: Pack voltage 300-407 V (EVSpecifications: 302 V 75 kWh, 346 V 85/90 kWh, 400-407 V 100 kWh; ArenaEV 300-360 V), well below 800 V: 400 V class.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: a Model S owner's manual (ManualsLib page 145, undated edition, quoted: "When navigating to a Supercharger location, Model S may allocate energy to pre-heat the Battery"); Electrek (2020.24.6 release note) gives the same behaviour for Model S/X in 2020 software. No page says whether every MCU1-era car (2012-2017) runs it, and cars ordered without navigation (Tech Package; TMC thread 2019-03-07) probably do not. No manual battery control found. tesla.com manuals are 403.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: EVSpecifications gives 90 kW for 2012 and 120 kW for 2014 (85 kWh); 2013 carried over from 2014 (unproven: 2012 was lower).

ac_max_kw.notes: Tesla 2012-2020 Model S service manual VIN reference, 2012-2013 digit 7 "Charger Type": "A" = "10 kW Charger", "B" = "20 kW Charger", "C"/"D" the same with DC fast charge. The single 10 kW charger is the standard fitment, the 20 kW dual charger an option (Wikipedia: two onboard chargers optional before 2016); not a Signature-specific finding. EVSpecifications lists 11.5 kW (240 V 48 A) for 2012 but that looks generic.
